digest.component_or_area: Cloud adapter parity with DC—resilience and config validation
propositions: Cloud lacks per-member 429 sweep enumeration across four distinct retry behaviors (direct REST no-retry, subprocess rate-limit-backoff, dispatch-wrapper retry, non-retrying apply-phases), leaving mutations vulnerable to undocumented or newly-introduced retry paths that could cause duplicates.

Cloud has no config-validation tier testing for non-HTTPS URLs, missing credentials, or scheme rejection, whereas DC enforces both via post-init validation and tests for silent anonymous fallback (bug cd78 analog).

Cloud's probe hardcodes RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES rather than threading resolved_statuses from config at runtime, preventing Cloud deployments with non-standard Jira workflow status names from being probed correctly without code changes.
DC user-search method aliases are absent, so DC transport should degrade to string-matching on assignable-search rather than raising, but this degradation is untested.

Every mutating Cloud transport member must be explicitly classified on two axes (transport seam and dispatch level) with duplicate-write safety assessment for each, establishing which retry behaviors are intentional and which are undiscovered bugs.

Existing tests incompletely cover the 429 surface: test_retry_httperror.py and test_acli_subprocess_timeout.py:352–368 do not enumerate all mutating members or assert attempt counts at proper boundaries, risking silent inheritance of untested retry by later-added mutations.
